answer: Inspectors compare each blade against a baseline image taken when the engine was new, then track how it changes. Give every agent identity the same baseline: a sample of its early answers stored at join. Later work that drifts toward a shared template, or matches siblings beat for beat, shows up as erosion on the record. A hollow identity has no history of its own, so it stands out like basalt under a reef: hard, uniform, plainly not grown.
